status.summary: Active, coming off a loss. Quillan Salkilld submitted him with a rear-naked choke at 4:25 of round 1 in the UFC Vegas 120 main event (Aug 8, 2026). Before that he submitted Esteban Ribovics with an arm-triangle at UFC 327 (Apr 11, 2026), and in Oct 2025 Charles Oliveira submitted him in Rio. He is 2-2 in his last four; pro record 26-5 (1 NC). On Sep 12, 2026 he also lost his opening-round match at the ADCC World Championships in Krakow to Elijah Dorsey (rear-naked choke). He is #10 in the UFC's media-panel rankings and #9 in its Meta rankings. No bout is announced: on Oct 26 he said he had accepted a UFC offer for the first quarter of 2027 without naming the opponent or date, and denied a rumoured January fight with Axel Sola; on Nov 5 he answered Tom Nolan's call-out with 'Bierzemy' ('we'll take it'). He says a cut on his nose from before the Salkilld fight keeps reopening.

style.summary: A wrestler who wins on takedown volume. He shoots almost four times as often as the median lightweight, holds top position for about a third of his fight time, and finishes with ground strikes or chokes from top. Standing, he lands little but is hard to hit cleanly. His recent losses came against elite grapplers who took his back in scrambles.

engine_notes.note: Takedown volume is the core skill: 13.3 attempts per 15 min career at 38% (5.1 landed per 15; lightweight medians about 3.6 attempted and 1.2 landed), 11.8 attempts at 42% recency-weighted.
Top-control share: 285 control seconds per 15 min career and 332 recency-weighted (32-37% of fight time; median about 17%). Opponents control him only 7-10% of the time.

Knocked down 5 times in 159.5 minutes (Kutateladze, Tsarukyan, Dariush, Turner, Dos Anjos; 0.47 per 15) but 0 KO/TKO losses in 14 UFC fights, so knockdowns should not convert into finishes at the usual rate.

Submission risk comes from scrambles rather than off his back: both MMA submission losses came after the opponent took his back (Oliveira R2 2:48, Salkilld R1 4:25), and Elijah Dorsey also took his back and choked him in the first round of ADCC 2026 (Sep 12, 2026).

Five-round pace evidence is thin: the pace curve (1.00 / 2.45 / 2.68 / 1.74 / 2.68) shows output rising after round 1, but rounds 3-5 rest on one fight (Tsarukyan, 2022). Treat late-round claims as uncertain.
